steps.name: Prepare ranked gene list and validate DE results table
steps.question: How many of the 12000 tested genes in de_results.csv have a valid Wald statistic usable for ranking, and how many were excluded (NA) due to DESeq2 outlier flagging or independent filtering?
steps.description: Load de_results.csv (12000 genes x 8 columns: gene, base_mean, log2_fold_change, log2_fold_change shrunken variant, stat/Wald statistic, p-value, padj, etc.), verify presence of a Wald statistic column and gene symbol column, drop rows with NA stat (DESeq2 outlier-flagged or independent-filtering-excluded genes), and report how many of the 12000 tested genes have a usable ranking statistic. Report the count of genes with NA padj (independent filtering / Cook's outlier flag) separately from genes actually excluded from the rank.
acceptance_criteria: Ranked gene list built from de_results.csv stat column, one value per gene, duplicates resolved
Count of genes with NA stat/padj reported separately from genes with a valid rank
Output is a two-column table (gene symbol, Wald statistic) sorted descending, saved for the enrichment step

steps.name: fgsea preranked GSEA against MSigDB Hallmark
steps.question: Which of the 50 MSigDB Hallmark pathways are significantly enriched (up or down) in psoriasis lesional vs control skin, ranked by the DESeq2 Wald statistic from the treated-vs-control contrast?

grounding.reason: fgsea preranked GSEA on the Wald statistic with MSigDB Hallmark per R-0098/R-0107/R-0048; rank metric choice (stat) stated per disputed rule R-0108

steps.description: Run fgsea preranked gene set enrichment on the DESeq2 Wald-statistic-ranked full gene list (all ~12000 tested genes, no pre-thresholding) against the MSigDB human Hallmark gene set collection (50 sets, HGNC symbols, staged at /mnt/refs/managed/msigdb-hallmark-human/2026.1/h.all.v2026.1.Hs.symbols.gmt). Apply gene set size window 15-500 after intersecting with tested genes, Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment across the 50 tested hallmark sets, collapse redundant significant sets (fgsea::collapsePathways or gseaResTable equivalent), and report leading-edge genes for each significant set (padj < 0.05).
acceptance_criteria: fgsea run on the full ranked list of tested genes, not a thresholded subset
Gene set size window 15-500 applied and stated
Results table has NES, pval, padj, size, and leading-edge genes per hallmark set
Significant sets (padj<0.05) collapsed for redundancy with full table kept as supplement
Ranking metric (Wald statistic) and gene set collection version (MSigDB 2026.1 Hallmark) stated in output

steps.name: fgsea preranked GSEA against Reactome pathways (cross-check)
steps.question: Which specific Reactome pathways are enriched in psoriasis lesional vs control skin, and how do they map onto or diverge from the significant MSigDB Hallmark pathways found in T2S1?

grounding.reason: Human: Reactome is the second collection after Hallmark, per R-0098

steps.description: Run the same preranked fgsea (same Wald-statistic ranking, same 15-500 size window) against the Reactome human pathway gene sets (staged at /mnt/refs/managed/reactome-pathways/current/ReactomePathways.gmt, filtered to Homo sapiens using ReactomePathways.txt species column) as the second-pass, more granular collection per the standard human enrichment workflow. Report overlap and disagreement between the Hallmark-significant sets and the Reactome-significant sets covering the same genes/leading edges.
acceptance_criteria: Reactome GMT filtered to Homo sapiens before the test
Same ranking metric and size window as the Hallmark run
Report states overlap/divergence between Hallmark and Reactome significant results
Reactome release version noted (staged as 'current')

steps.question: What is the consolidated, reproducible summary of which hallmark pathways (and corroborating Reactome pathways) distinguish psoriasis lesional from control skin?

steps.description: Synthesize the Hallmark and Reactome fgsea results into a single report: significant hallmark pathways (padj<0.05) with direction (NES sign, up in lesional vs up in control), leading-edge genes per significant set, the Reactome cross-check overlap, and a reproducibility record (package versions for fgsea/R, gene set collection versions, random seed used for fgsea permutations, the ranking metric choice and rationale, the universe of tested genes, and the size window). State explicitly that enrichment results are method-dependent and should be read as hypotheses, and note the upstream caveat that sample_01 had library size ~4x below median in the original DE run.
acceptance_criteria: Report lists all significant hallmark sets with NES, padj, leading-edge genes
Report states gene set database name+version, ranking metric, universe, and size window used
Report includes a reproducibility record (session info, seed, package/collection versions)
Report explicitly flags method-dependence of enrichment results and the sample_01 library-size caveat

plan.title: Psoriasis lesional vs control hallmark pathway GSEA
plan.analytical_narrative: DESeq2 differential expression (treated=lesional vs control, 6 vs 6, unpaired, single batch) is already complete in de_results.csv (12000 genes tested). The research question asks which hallmark pathways change between conditions. Per the DE-to-enrichment procedure for human bulk RNA-seq: rank every tested gene by the DESeq2 Wald statistic (signed, variance-scaled — avoids the noise of unshrunken log2FC and the tie-saturation problem of signed p-values) and run fgsea preranked GSEA against the MSigDB Hallmark human collection (50 sets, staged locally), which is the standard first pass for 'which broad pathway changed'. A second pass against Reactome (staged locally, current release) resolves any hallmark hit to a specific curated pathway and serves as a cross-method check (rule: methods disagree, do not treat one result as ground truth). Gene identifiers (symbols in de_results.csv) are checked against both GMT collections directly since both are HGNC-symbol GMTs; no ID re-mapping to Entrez is required for fgsea run on symbols, but the unmapped share against each collection is reported. Size window 15-500 genes per set is applied after intersecting each set with the 12000 tested genes; redundant significant sets are collapsed and leading-edge genes reported for each retained set. The sample_01 library-size caveat (4x below median) does not affect this step directly since DE is already computed, but it is noted in the report as a caveat on the upstream DE result the ranking is built from.

steps.method: fgsea preranked GSEA on the DESeq2 Wald statistic against MSigDB Hallmark (human)
fgsea preranked GSEA on the DESeq2 Wald statistic against Reactome pathways (human-filtered)
Enrichment summary report with leading-edge genes and reproducibility record
